doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

chapter: Marriage and freelancing in New York
title: Memorable sessions, April in Paris wrong notes, perfectionism and Kristen
summary: Wrong notes on an April in Paris intro; perfectionism passed on to his daughter, a composer and drummer.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Can you recall a session that was particularly memorable either because it was really difficult and that you barely made it through it, or because it was so utterly ridiculous, like the story you just told me, music-wise maybe it was like really silly?

Well there were a lot of silly dates, but I don’t think about those. I think about the hard ones, the ones where I just about made, and the ones where I may have made a mistake and wasn’t too proud of it. But there was one date we did, the opening — I shouldn’t tell this one — the introduction to “April in Paris.” And I thought that we were just fooling

around and they were setting up the mics for balance. I played a couple of wrong notes in the intro. I didn’t know it until the record came out. But of course you couldn’t hear it unless you separated the channels and listened very carefully. I was personally embarrassed. I’ve never told this story. But there’s a couple of wrong notes I played on it.
Well, when you look at your career as a whole, I think a couple of wrong notes, we can live with that.
I’m starting to live with it now.
I take it you were a perfectionist.

Yeah, that’s part of my undoing. I was a perfectionist, my wife was a perfectionist, and some of it has rubbed off on my daughter except we took pains to let her know that she doesn’t have to do everything perfectly. And she’s done very well. She’s a published composer, she plays all the percussion instruments, she loves to play piano for fun, and her favorite thing is to sing. But I’m very proud of Kristen, so is her mother.
Yeah. And she is a good drummer.
